# CODING-HERMES-DIRECTOR — DATA MODEL & DUCKBRAIN KEY LAYOUT
``` DOC : contracts/DATA-MODEL.md REV : 1.4 (R31 revision pass 2026-11-09). Delta vs 1.3: explicit four-class routing namespaces and controller-authoritative coordination/control semantics (R31-028); peer provenance is defined by VOL-C/VOL-D (R31-029). Delta vs 1.2: §1.5 report v3 envelope/content variants and §1.5.1 ReportDataset/ReportRow logical records (R31-030); v3 freshness/retry precedence; report/dataset keys and ER diagram updated. Prior §1.6/§1.9/§1.10 changes remain cumulative. DATE : 2026-11-09 IMPLEMENTS: DESIGN.md v2 §3.2 (config registry), §4.4 (chat semantics), §4.5 (report contract), CT-01/CT-05/CT-09 AMENDED-BY: VOL-B rev 2.1 (record schemas, key normalization, ordering, restore procedure). On conflict, VOL-B controls. STATUS : CONTRACT. No server exists yet; this is what the build must conform to. Config surface = contracts/config.schema.json. ```
Data-class namespaces are explicit and never interchangeable. The controller coordination/report and protected control-key classes use the controller's **`chd`** namespace; native session archives use **`chd-archive`**; optional project/code memory uses a deployment-selected namespace. All room/registry/ send/report keys are controller-authoritative DuckBrain keys under `chd`, written through the harness service with role tokens (DESIGN FACT-19/FACT-20). A project-memory write is never a report/control acknowledgement. Effective backend, namespace, sync and grant are read back through `/v1/effective-routing`.
Namespace for control keys below: **`chd`** (the director namespace).
---
## 1. Entities

### 1.1 Agent
A hierarchy participant. Config data, operator-owned (CT-01, R-001). Never agent-editable (§6.3).
| Field | Type | Constraint | Meaning | |-------|------|-----------|---------| | `id` | string | `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` | Stable identity; used in `from`/`to`, registry key, bond key | | `role` | enum | `director \| manager \| supervisor` | Determines grants (DESIGN §6.1) and which room kinds it may create | | `gateway` | string | must match a `gateway.id` | **Binding** (RL-2/RL-7): the one gateway the agent runs on | | `workdir` | string (abs path) | — | Where the agent's sessions run | | `skills` | string[] | non-empty for all roles | Skill list the harness injects into the gateway (RL-2) | | `tools.include` / `tools.exclude` | string[] | deny by default (§6.1) | Tool rulesets; exclude wins | | `model` | string | non-empty | Explicit model id; no provider defaults | | `context_limit` | int | ≥ 1 | Context window cap in tokens | | `max_turns` | int | ≥ 1 | Per-session turn cap | | `token_budget` | int | ≥ 1 | Per-session token budget | | `max_sessions` | int | ≥ 1 | Concurrent bonded sessions allowed for this agent | | `max_parallel` | object | per room kind | Per-type parallel caps: `{objective, task, space}`, each int ≥ 0 | | `responsibility` | string | non-empty for manager/director | Registry entry (RL-8), mirrored to `chd/registry/<id>` | | `session` | object | see §1.6 | Bonding + reuse policy | | `triggers` | string[] | cron expressions | Registered as normal scheduler lanes (CT-02); `[]` = woken by messages only | | `rooms` | string[] | room ids or `task-<id>-*` globs | Membership; config data, never discovered (§4.6) |

### 1.2 Gateway
One addressable Hermes gateway (DESIGN §9). Host routing and concurrency are decided in ONE place — the gateway row.
| Field | Type | Constraint | Meaning | |-------|------|-----------|---------| | `id` | string | `^gw-[a-z0-9-]+$` | Referenced by `agent.gateway` | | `url` | string | `^https?://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:\d+)?$` | Gateway POST target | | `transport` | enum | `loopback \| tailscale \| ssh-tunnel \| direct` | How the harness reaches the host; never fails over silently | | `auth_token_ref` | string | non-empty | Reference to the credential file for this gateway | | `max_inflight` | int | ≥ 1 | **The backpressure** (RL-7): max concurrent agent requests on this gateway; sends beyond it queue, never dispatch |

### 1.3 Room
An objective, a task, or a manager-to-manager space. **A room IS a DuckBrain key family** — one ordered, searchable log (RL-4/RL-5/RL-6).
| Field | Type | Constraint | Meaning | |-------|------|-----------|---------| | `id` | string | `^(obj\|task\|space)-[a-z0-9-]+$` | Room id; key family is `chd/room/<id>/<seq>` | | `kind` | enum | `objective \| task \| space` | objective = director+managers (RL-4); task = manager+supervisors (RL-5); space = managers↔managers, registry-justified (RL-8) | | `participants` | string[] | agent ids; ≥ 2; kind-consistent | Membership is config data + registry justification (CT-09) |
Kind rules: `objective` must contain exactly one director; `task` must not contain a director; `space` must contain only managers, each with a `registry` entry (router refuses otherwise, CT-09).

### 1.4 Message
One entry in a room's log. JSON at key `chd/room/<room-id>/<seq>` (DESIGN §4.4).
| Field | Type | Constraint | Meaning | |-------|------|-----------|---------| | `room` | string | existing room id | Key family this seq belongs to | | `seq` | int | ≥ 1, monotonic per room | Server-allocated; race-safety per UQ-7/OQ-14 (harness single-writer if needed) | | `from` | string | `owner` or member agent id | Attribution; owner posts with no self-echo (RL-6) | | `to` | string | agent id \| `group` \| `@<agent-id>` | Decides **who is WOKEN**, not who can read — the log is visible to all members | | `thread` | int (optional) | seq of root message | Sub-thread; threads are reads over the same log, nothing stored outside it | | `kind` | enum | `msg \| question \| status \| directive \| task \| report \| incident` | The complete seven-value enum (R31-003; identical in VOL-B §3.1, VOL-C §3.2/§3.6). `question` = answer owed in-thread (missing-reply detection); `status` = progress/state post; `directive` opens an objective; `task` opens a task room/subthread; `report` carries a report attachment; `incident` is a service-written escalation record (R-017). Per-role/per-room legality is the single table in VOL-C §3.6 (VOLC-066) | | `body` | string | non-empty | Human-readable text | | `attach` | object[] (optional) | report refs | `kind=report` messages carry the report JSON here (RL-6) | | `ts` | string | RFC 3339 UTC | Write timestamp |
Storage amendment (VOL-B §3.1, R31 revision): the ambiguous optional `thread` field is replaced by the explicit pair `thread_root` (stable grouping key) and `reply_to` (tree edge), and `dedupe_key`/`send_id` are promoted into indexed attributes. VOL-B §3.1 is the storage-normative shape; this table stays the entity-level view and carries the same kind enum verbatim.

### 1.5 Report (schema v3)
A finished task's report **arrives as a chat message** with one common envelope and exactly one requester-selected content variant. The authoritative contract is `contracts/schemas/report-v3.schema.json`; the same envelope persists `class=free_form`, `class=structured`, or `class=dataset` content in DuckBrain. The v2 shape below is superseded and accepted only through migration.
| Envelope field | Type | Constraint | Meaning | |---|---|---|---| | `id` | string | `^r-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9]+$` | Immutable report id | | `produced_by` / `room` | string | member agent / room id | Producer and posting room | | `send_id` / `attempt_id` | string | existing grammars | Logical send and dispatch attempt | | `request_ref` | string | `/chd/room/<room>/m<seq>` | Exact request message | | `session_ref` | object | `{mode: NEW\|REUSE, session_key}` | Session correlation | | `status` / `summary` | enum / string | status vocabulary; summary non-empty | Outcome and human roll-up | | `assignment` | object | required_content, schema_ref, validation_policy, completion_policy | Immutable requester contract | | `content_ref` / `content_digest` | string | DuckBrain key / sha256 | Content identity | | `ingest_ts` | string | harness-recorded RFC 3339 UTC | Trusted freshness clock |
Content variants are: `free_form` (non-empty `text`), `structured` (JSON object validated by immutable `schema_ref={name,version,digest}`), and `dataset` (ReportDataset + typed ReportRow records). Unknown schema is `422 schema_unsupported`; invalid data is `422 schema_validation`.
**Freshness rule v3 (supersedes CHD-3 and v2 wording).** Freshness is `ingest_ts >= dispatch_ts` for the same `(send_id, attempt_id, session_ref)`; agent `ts` and timestamps within an attachment are evidence only. A stale attachment in a newly accepted envelope is reviewed as evidence, not rejected as an old report. Mismatched attempt/session is `bad_report{reason: attempt_mismatch}` or `wrong_request`. Only a carrier accepted and durably persisted by the harness exists for verification. A send with no report inside its deadline is `no_report` and enters the ladder.
**Single precedence.** Exact replay of the same attempt and content digest is a dedupe response; a different second report while open is `409 report_already_posted`; a non-replay report after terminal closure is recorded `duplicate_ignored`; a late valid result may close only still-open work. The complete first-match table is VOL-D VOLD-026; this entity contract does not define another duplicate rule.

### 1.5.1 ReportDataset and ReportRow
`ReportDataset` and `ReportRow` are logical records stored as JSON memories in DuckBrain, not a dependency on an unreleased declared-table API. Dataset keys are `/chd/dataset/<send-id>/<dataset-id>` and `/chd/dataset/<send-id>/<dataset-id>/r<row:08d>`.
| Entity | Required fields and rules | |---|---| | `ReportDataset` | `dataset_id`, `report_id` (exactly one), `send_id`, `schema_ref`, ordered `columns` (`string\|integer\|number\|boolean\|timestamp\|json` + nullable), `row_count`, `state=staging\|published\|failed`, `retention_days`, `published_ts`; immutable after publish | | `ReportRow` | `dataset_id`, dense harness-assigned `row_id=r00000001` onward, `values` typed against columns, optional `row_ts`; unique and immutable within dataset |
Only `state=published` datasets are readable. The service enforces report-read permission; unauthorized callers get indistinguishable `404 not_found`. Query uses a closed typed `filter`, deterministic `order_by` + row_id, `page_size` 1..500, and opaque keyset `cursor`; returns `rows`, `next_cursor`, and `has_more`. Partial uploads remain staging and expose neither rows nor report; validation failure is audited as `422 schema_validation` or `422 dataset_row_invalid`. A correction is a new dataset and report. A retry with the same attempt and content digest is an exact replay; a different digest uses the V3 second-report rule.

### 1.6 SessionBond
The bond between one agent and one Hermes session in the context of one room and one work branch (RL-4). **Identity (rev 1.2, R31-022/D-025):** the bond is NO longer one-per-agent or one-per-(agent × room). The bond identity and key grammar are:
``` bond identity : (agent, room, subthread_root, work_uid) + generation bond key : chd/bond/<agent-id>/<bond-id> bond_id : b-YYYYMMDD-HHMM-<rand> subthread_root: seq of the task/subthread root message; null for room-level work work_uid : ticket id, assignment id, or send id — the one work item the session owns (prevents two tasks sharing a session) generation : >= 1, incremented on session replacement (VOL-B §7.5) ```
The identity tuple **admits two concurrent tasks for the same agent in the same room**: the tuples differ in `(subthread_root, work_uid)`, so each task holds its own bond, its own thread, and its own Hermes session. The record is harness-owned runtime state (written by the harness, never by agents); the full record schema — `bond_id`, `generation`, `parent_bond_id`, `fork_mode`, `policy_snapshot_id`, `policy_rev`, `hermes_base_url`, `hermes_session_id`, `session_key`, `hermes_profile`, `state ∈ provisioned|active|retired|lost`, `runtime_caps`, `reuse_policy` — is VOL-B §3.3. `fork_mode` is the explicit D-038 mode; it is not inferred from the bond's generation or delivery mode.
**Worked example (normative; fixture VOLB-067).** Supervisor `sup-nova` holds two concurrent tasks in room `task-auth-14`. Both bonds are `active` simultaneously (requires `max_sessions >= 2`), with **two distinct bond ids and two distinct threads**:
| bond_id | agent | room | subthread_root | work_uid | gen | hermes_session_id | state | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | `b-20261109-0914-q4x7` | sup-nova | task-auth-14 | 42 | T-101 | 1 | `sess-aa11…` (its own session) | active | | `b-20261109-0917-m8k3` | sup-nova | task-auth-14 | 57 | T-205 | 1 | `sess-bb22…` (a different session) | active |
A reply or report posted under thread root `42` is owned by bond `b-…-q4x7` only; under `57`, by `b-…-m8k3` only (routing rule VOLB-063, VOL-B §7.5). Conversations cannot mix because Hermes scopes history by session id and CHD scopes wakes by bond.
| Field | Type | Constraint | Meaning | |-------|------|-----------|---------| | `agent` | string | agent id | Owner of the bonded session | | `room` | string | room id | The bonded room; every wake lands as a message in it | | `subthread_root` | int \| null | existing seq, or null | Which branch of the room this session serves | | `work_uid` | string | non-empty | The one work item this session owns | | `generation` | int | ≥ 1 | Replacement counter for the same identity tuple | | `session_key` | string | Hermes session key | Durable key the scheduler transmits (FACT-11); REUSE mode sends here | | `reuse_policy` | enum | `reuse-until-wedged \| always-new` | The ONLY config knob selecting between the two delivery modes NEW/REUSE (CT-04); there is no third mode | | `fork_mode` | enum \| null | `preserve_parent_snapshot \| current_policy`; null for a fresh non-forked session | D-038 mode selected at fork; readback returns it | | `policy_snapshot_id` | string \| null | existing snapshot id | SessionPolicySnapshot bound to the bond; CHD31-06 owns grant lineage records | | `policy_rev` | int \| null | >= 1 once snapshot exists | Effective revision returned by session-policy readback; resync increments atomically |

### 1.7 RegistryEntry
The responsibilities registry (RL-8, CT-09). Authoritative source is the config's per-agent `responsibility`; the **harness mirrors it** to `chd/registry/<agent-id>` (harness-written, agents read-only). A manager-to-manager `space` whose members lack registry entries is refused by the router.
| Field | Type | Meaning | |-------|------|---------| | `agent` | string | agent id | | `responsibility` | string | "who owns X" — human- and agent-readable | | `mirror_key` | string | `chd/registry/<agent-id>` |

### 1.8 Limit entries
Limits are config data with explicit minimums; they are the entire backpressure story (RL-7, DESIGN §3.4/§5.5).
| Limit | Scope | Field | Default floor | |-------|-------|-------|---------------| | Gateway concurrency | per gateway | `gateways[].max_inflight` ≥ 1 | sends beyond it queue, never dispatch | | Agent sessions | per agent | `agents[].max_sessions` ≥ 1 | concurrent bonded sessions | | Parallel work by room kind | per agent | `agents[].max_parallel.{objective,task,space}` ≥ 0 | 0 = the agent never holds that kind | | Fan-out | harness | `orchestration.max_fanout` ≥ 1 (default 12) | max wakes composed per cycle | | Send staleness | harness | `orchestration.stale_after_s` ≥ 60 | queued send older than this → `deferred{reason: backpressure}` | | Verify deadline | harness | `verify.deadline_s` ≥ 60 (default 1800) | inside gateway timeout 3600 (FACT-21) | | Remind cadence | harness | `verify.remind_gap_s` ≥ 30, `verify.max_reminds` ≥ 0 (default 2) | ladder rung 0 pacing |

### 1.10 ExportManifest (new in rev 1.2 — R31-016)
One record per committed native Hermes session-export checkpoint, in the **archive namespace `chd-archive`** (D-018: session exports and CHD control state use SEPARATE namespaces). CHD owns the manifest; the export payload's internal shape is Hermes' own and is **probed, never assumed** (OPEN-6). The committed JSON Schema is `contracts/schemas/session-archive.schema.json` (`$defs.exportManifest`); the storage-normative record is VOL-B §3.12.
| Field | Type | Constraint | Meaning | |-------|------|-----------|---------| | `manifest_id` | string | `em-YYYYMMDD-HHMM-<rand>` | Identity; immutable | | `session_archive_id` | string | existing §1.11 archive id | The per-session index this checkpoint belongs to | | `agent` / `profile` | string | existing config identity | Subject of the export | | `session_id` / `session_key` | string | Hermes identity | Exported session | | `bond_id` / `work_uid` | string \| null | existing | Work linkage | | `room` / `subthread_root` | string / int \| null | existing | Thread lineage | | `export_schema` | object | `{name: "hermes.session.export", version: "<probed>"}` | **Native format/version** — probed from the deployed Hermes, never guessed | | `checkpoint_id` | string | `ck-YYYYMMDD-HHMM-<rand>` | Identity of this coverage boundary | | `checkpoint_seq` | int | ≥ 1, monotone per session | Messages ≤ this seq are included | | `coverage` | object | `{from_ts, through_ts}` RFC 3339 UTC | The **coverage window** the payload claims | | `completeness` | enum | `complete \| partial \| declared_gap` | What the exporter claims; not `complete` ⇒ `gap_ref` MUST be set | | `gap_ref` | string \| null | archive key of a §1.10 gap record | **Gap marker** naming the declared gap; a silent partial export is a defect | | `payload_ref` / `payload_digest` / `bytes` | string / string / int | archive key / sha256 / ≥ 0 | The bytes and their integrity check | | `incremental` | object \| null | `{base_checkpoint_id, dedupe: "content_digest"}` | **Incremental dedupe**: an incremental export names the base checkpoint and dedupes rows by content digest against it | | `state` | enum | `staging \| committed \| superseded \| failed` | **Export status**: `committed` only after digest verification | | `failure_ref` | string \| null | archive key of the gap record | Set when `state=failed` — **failed-export visibility is a named record+field**, never a silent absence | | `retention_until` | string \| null | RFC 3339 UTC | Derived from archive retention policy |

### 1.9 Ticket (R31-017/R31-018; controller-authoritative)
A Ticket is the general-purpose shared work item. The controller ticket service owns its identity, graph, authorization, workflow binding, revision and state; DuckBrain stores the durable `TicketRecord` representation and immutable transition events under `/chd/ticket`. No board file, room message, report, or DuckBrain-linked evidence record owns those fields.
| Field | Type | Constraint | Meaning | |---|---|---|---| | `ticket_id` | string | registered `<family>-<nnn>`; never reused | Stable identity | | `title` / `kind` | string / enum | title non-empty; `task|bug|review|decision|incident|epic` | Generic work category, including non-coding work | | `workflow` | object | `{workflow_id, version, machine_ref, state_projection}` | Binding to `build-spec/state-machines.json`; not a second machine | | `state` | string | controller projection of objective or assignment machine | Current workflow state | | `parent_id` / `depends_on` | string[] | existing ids; acyclic | Parent/child and prerequisite links | | `accountable_owner` | string | exactly one agent id | Sole accountable owner | | `assignees` / `watchers` | string[] | agent ids | Actors and observers | | `criteria` | object[] | criterion id, text, provenance, version, evidence refs | Acceptance conditions | | `authorization` | object | required grants, actor scope, approval ref | Mutation/dispatch authorization facts | | `links` | object | objective, room, thread, sends, reports, artifacts | Correlation and evidence links | | `priority` / `revision` | integer | priority 0–9; revision ≥ 1 and monotone | Ordering and CAS | | `created_ts` / `updated_ts` / `closed_ts` | RFC 3339 string | timestamps | Lifecycle times | | `meta` | object | optional | Source and correlation metadata |
Each transition atomically increments `revision` and appends `/chd/ticket/<ticket-id>/event/m<seq:012d>` with `from`, `to`, actor, reason, revision before/after, evidence refs and timestamp. A stale revision returns `409 ticket_revision_conflict` with no write. On restart, the controller reloads the highest committed TicketRecord revision and ordered events. The linked ObjectiveRecord, AssignmentRecord, RoomMessage, SendManifest, Report and artifacts are evidence or projections only; they do not compete for authority.

### 1.11 SessionArchive (new in rev 1.2 — R31-016)
The durable per-session index of exported checkpoints — the record a **replacement host** queries to discover and read a lost host's sessions (D-017). Stored in namespace `chd-archive`; written only by the archive ingestor (a harness-side principal holding its own credential — no agent ever holds an archive credential). Committed JSON Schema: `contracts/schemas/session-archive.schema.json` (`$defs.sessionArchive`).
| Field | Type | Constraint | Meaning | |-------|------|-----------|---------| | `archive_id` | string | `sa-YYYYMMDD-HHMM-<rand>` | Identity | | `agent` / `profile` | string | existing config identity | Subject | | `session_id` / `session_key` | string | Hermes identity | Archived session | | `bond_ids` / `work_uids` | string[] | existing bond ids / work items | Bonds that served this session over its life | | `rooms` / `subthread_roots` | string[] / int[] | existing | Thread lineage summary | | `latest_checkpoint_id` / `latest_checkpoint_seq` | string / int | from the newest committed manifest | Newest committed coverage boundary | | `covered_through_ts` | string | RFC 3339 UTC | Newest committed `coverage.through_ts` | | `manifest_count` | int | ≥ 0 | Committed ExportManifests for this session | | `open_gaps` | string[] | gap record keys | Unresolved declared gaps / failed exports | | `state` | enum | `active \| frozen \| expired` | Lifecycle; `expired` = past retention | | `retention_until` | string \| null | RFC 3339 UTC | Retention bound | | `ts` | string | RFC 3339 UTC | Last index update |
**Discovery and access (normative).** Replacement discovery is by `(agent, profile)` prefix scan over `/sessions/<agent>/<profile>/` (query contract VOL-B §5.10). Every archive read — including a replacement's — requires an explicit archive read grant (VOL-C §8.8); **there is no implicit read**. The grant-record schema and selector grammar for archive scopes are owned by **CHD31-06**; archive read MUST NOT ship ahead of that record.
**Hard limitation (normative).** An archived record is NEVER evidence that a live session exists or can be resumed. Restore is a validated IMPORT into a new local session store (VOL-B §5.10/VOLB-070, VOL-D §5.2), never a resumption of the archived session or a copy of a live database.
---

## 2. DuckBrain key layout (namespace `chd`)
| Key | Writer | Content | |-----|--------|---------| | `chd/room/<room-id>/<seq>` | harness service (controller-authoritative) | Message JSON (§1.4); `kind=report` carries the report object as attachment | | `chd/registry/<agent-id>` | **harness only** | RegistryEntry mirror (CT-09) | | `chd/delegation/<delegation-id>` | **harness only** | DelegationRecord (§3.6 VOL-B): bounded authority and lineage | | `chd/send/<send-id>/manifest` | **harness only** | Send composition record: send_id, room, target, mode NEW/REUSE, gateway, dispatch_ts, deadline, verify outcome, close reason | | `chd/ticket/<ticket-id>` | **controller ticket service** | TicketRecord (§1.9); controller-authoritative shared work state | | `chd/ticket/<ticket-id>/event/m<seq:012d>` | **controller ticket service** | Immutable Ticket transition event (§1.9) | | `chd/bond/<agent-id>/<bond-id>` | **harness only** | SessionBond record (§1.6): identity `(agent, room, subthread_root, work_uid)` + generation, session refs, state | | `chd/report/<send-id>/<report-id>` | **harness only** | Schema-v3 report envelope plus one content variant (§1.5) | | `chd/dataset/<send-id>/<dataset-id>` | **harness only** | ReportDataset descriptor (§1.5.1) | | `chd/dataset/<send-id>/<dataset-id>/r<row:08d>` | **harness only** | ReportRow with typed values (§1.5.1) |
**Archive namespace `chd-archive` (rev 1.2 — R31-016; D-018 separates it from the `chd` control namespace).** Canonical leading-slash form per VOLB-003; writer for every row is the **archive ingestor only** — the harness never writes it and no agent holds an archive credential:
| Key | Content | |-----|---------| | `/sessions/<agent>/<profile>/<session-id>` | SessionArchive index (§1.10) | | `/sessions/<agent>/<profile>/<session-id>/<checkpoint-id>/export.json` | Native Hermes export payload | | `/sessions/<agent>/<profile>/<session-id>/<checkpoint-id>/manifest` | ExportManifest (§1.9) | | `/sessions/<agent>/<profile>/<session-id>/<checkpoint-id>/policy` | SessionPolicySnapshot copy for restore (VOL-B §3.11) | | `/gaps/<agent>/<profile>/<session-id>/<checkpoint-id>` | ArchiveGapRecord — declared coverage gap or failed export (§1.9 `gap_ref`/`failure_ref`) |
Patterns (enforced by `config.schema.json` and the harness write gate):
- room id: `^(obj|task|space)-[a-z0-9-]+$` - room key: `^chd/room/(obj|task|space)-[a-z0-9-]+/[0-9]+$` - registry key: `^chd/registry/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` - send key: `^chd/send/s-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9]+/manifest$` - bond key: `^chd/bond/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*/b-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9]+$` - archive session key: `^/sessions/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*/[^/]+$` - general duckbrain key: `^chd/[a-z0-9-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)*$`

## 4. Complete operation-facing inventory
`build-spec/VOL-E-operation-reference.md` §5 is the bidirectional operation-facing inventory of every namespace, key family and query path in this document. It does not replace the field tables above. The control namespace is `chd`; the archive namespace is `chd-archive`; the writer is the harness/controller except archive rows, which are archive-ingestor-only. Every record family has a canonical key, required field table, indexed attributes and at least one prefix/query example.

### 4.1 Field and namespace invariants
All control records are JSON content with `rev` where the family is state-carrying, RFC 3339 `ts`, and a service writer identity. Indexed attributes are projections used for filtering and never a second source of truth. `/chd/room/*`, `/chd/send/*`, `/chd/report/*`, `/chd/ticket/*`, `/chd/grant/*`, `/chd/audit/*`, `/chd/wait/*`, `/chd/objective/*`, `/chd/assignment/*`, `/chd/bond/*`, `/chd/registry/*`, `/chd/limits/*`, `/chd/policy/*`, `/chd/rule/*`, `/chd/acceptance/*`, `/chd/aggregation/*`, `/chd/dataset/*` and `/chd/pattern/*` are control families. `/sessions/*`, `/gaps/*` and checkpoint children are archive families. Agents have no direct write credential for either namespace.

### 4.2 Query examples
The implementation uses DuckBrain HTTP prefix/keyset access, not an assumed declared-table API: `GET /api/memories?namespace=chd&prefix=/chd/room/<room>/&limit=500`; `GET /api/memories?namespace=chd&prefix=/chd/send/&attr.state=open`; `GET /api/memories?namespace=chd&prefix=/chd/ticket/<id>/event/&attr.seq_gt=<n>`; `GET /api/memories?namespace=chd-archive&prefix=/sessions/<agent>/<profile>/`; and `GET /api/memories?namespace=chd-archive&prefix=/gaps/<agent>/`. Query authorization is checked before the prefix is exposed; inaccessible targets return `404 not_found` and an authorized audit record. Dataset rows use typed keyset pagination and never offset pagination.
